thread:
jen: Heads-up — PR #5499 (microbatch/kvcache tweaks) is flagged by the perf CI. p95 latency jumped ~12% on longseq runs. Can the owners take a quick look before we decide canary vs revert? https://ci.internal/bench/5499 :eyes:

sasha: Thanks for the ping. Which workload saw the regression? long-seq only or also chat/short seq?

jen: long-seq 2k tokens primarily. short-seq (64-256) looks fine. Throughput dropped a bit on empty-cache runs.

kevin: tagging me — I'll check kernel selection changes in the PR.

maria: curious if KV eviction heuristics changed? PR mentions microbatch scheduling + kv-prefetch tweak.

bench-bot: Attached benchmark summary for PR #5499:

```
workload    baseline(ms p95)    pr5499(ms p95)    delta
long-seq    210                235                +11.9%
chat-64     32                 33                 +3%
throughput  420 req/s           390 req/s           -7%
memory      12.1GB             12.4GB             +0.3GB
```

bench-bot: Full flamegraphs & artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/5499/bench-zip

tae: quick read — looks like contention in the KV cache lock for long seq when batch sizes spike. I see more locking in the trace.

kevin: yeah, kernel selector change shouldn't affect locking. Prob the microbatch merge timing increased simultaneous kv access.

maria: If it's locking, a short-term revert might be safest for SLAs. But if the change reduces tail for other workloads we could tweak scheduling.

jen: We have a canary window tonight 22:00 UTC. Decision needed by 19:00 to revert first thing. Can reviewers give green/red?

sasha: I'll do a pass on the PR diff in 30m. Marking as high priority.

kevin: Quick notes from code skim: the new `merge_batches()` adds an extra loop that can coalesce >8 microbatches into one lock-critical section. I can propose a patch to move the merge outside the kv lock. If acceptable, that might fix p95.

jen: That would be ideal. Can you open a follow-up PR with the patch? We can bench it in a fast canary if ready.

kevin: Will do. ETA 2 hours.

maria: If Kevin's patch arrives, can we run a focused long-seq bench only (no concurrent workloads) to isolate? Bench-bot, please queue long-seq 2k with empty cache + full cache.

bench-bot: queued: long-seq-2k-empty, long-seq-2k-warm. Expected completion ~ 18:45 UTC.

tae: +1 on focused bench. Revert plan is the fallback.

jen: Cool. Sasha / Maria, if Kevin's patch fixes numbers we can keep PR and push canary. If not, revert and rework.

sasha: Reading now. Small comment on the locking wrapper already in PR, I'll post inline.

kevin: opened follow-up PR #5502 with proposed move of merge out of kv lock: https://git.internal/r/5502

jen: Thanks. Kevin — can you add a microbenchmark of the critical section (before/after) in the PR description? Helps reviewers.

kevin: Added simple microbench results in the PR: `before 1.8ms avg lock hold` -> `after 0.7ms avg`.

bench-bot: PR #5502 queued for same long-seq bench as #5499 diff. Results will be posted when available.

maria: if bench shows improvement, can we still hit canary tonight? Need @deploy-bot approval window too.

deploy-bot: Canary window request received. Manual approval required for deploys after 21:30 UTC.

jen: Ok. Plan: wait for #5502 bench. If p95 delta drops <3% and throughput recovers within 5%, schedule canary at 22:00. If not, revert #5499 at 19:30. Everyone OK? :thumbsup:

sasha: :thumbsup: I'll finish reviews before 19:00.

kevin: will monitor bench.

maria: ack. If revert happens, I'll prepare rollback notes for SRE.

bench-bot: long-seq-2k results for #5502 vs baseline:

```
workload    baseline(ms p95)    pr5502(ms p95)    delta
long-seq    210                215                +2.4%
throughput  420 req/s           410 req/s           -2.4%
memory      12.1GB             12.3GB             +0.2GB
```

jen: These look acceptable. Sasha, wanna re-run your review with the new patch?

sasha: Skimmed — LGTM pending one nit. Approving on principle for canary.

maria: I'll stand by for canary monitoring. If we see any tail regressions, we'll auto-revert.

jen: Great — scheduling canary at 22:00 UTC. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

kevin: nice team effort :pray:

bench-bot: Canary deployment started at 22:00 UTC. Will report metrics in #eng-runtime-canary channel.

jen: Closing this thread, will post results in canary channel. Good work!
